subject: POC success criteria & trial plan - Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodai.com>
To: Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@atlas-payments.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: POC success criteria & trial plan - Atlas Payments

Thanks again for the time today - really appreciate the clear context on Atlas Payments' primary goals. Following up with a short recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the trial plan.

Recap (from our call):
- Primary objective: validate inference economics and accuracy for our fraud classification/ NLP augmentation flows in production-like conditions.
- Workload profile: 2-3K daily inference requests, 95th percentile latency sensitivity, mixed short (prompt ~50 tokens) and medium (prompt ~400 tokens) requests.
- Important integrations: Datadog for metrics and SSO for admin access.

Proposed POC success criteria (draft):
- Latency: P95 <= 200 ms for short requests; P95 <= 450 ms for medium requests (measured from Redwood endpoint in us-west).
- Throughput: sustained 50 qps with <5% error rate during peak burst windows.
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0005 under the trial workload (we'll provide cost breakdown).
- Quality: >= 90% pass rate against a 100-item golden set (human-reviewed), and no more than a 5% drop in key classification F1 relative to baseline.

Evaluation plan and timeline (proposed):
- Trial length: 2 weeks (we can extend to 3 weeks if you prefer)  - target kickoff Mon, Jul 20.
- Redwood deliverables: dedicated trial environment (endpoint + keys), dashboards (latency/cost/throughput), Datadog metrics export, and a short-run training on using the dashboard.
- Atlas deliverables: share sample prompts & expected labels (we referenced a 100-item golden set on the call), provide a point-of-contact and test traffic window for peak simulation.
- Ownership: Jordan (AE) will coordinate logistics; Marissa (CS) will run the onboarding and trial ops.

Next steps:
1) Confirm sample prompt upload and preferred trial length (2 vs 3 weeks).
2) I'll send the trial agreement and set a kickoff calendar invite for the week of Jul 20.
3) Share the golden set CSV to the Drive link below.

Attachments: POC-success-criteria.xlsx, redwood-trial-plan.pdf
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-atlas-poc
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/deal/DEAL-2026-0812

Thanks - happy to adjust anything above.

-
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: POC success criteria & trial plan - Atlas Payments

Jordan - thanks for the clear recap. This looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying items before we lock the kickoff: 

1) Latency measurement: is the P95 target measured end-to-end from the Redwood endpoint (i.e., excluding our client-side network)? We're primarily interested in what our customers will see from our US-West app.
2) Quality metric: we have a 200-item test set (not 100) that includes edge cases - can Redwood run evaluation on that instead?
3) Datadog: can Redwood push trial metrics into our Datadog account (we prefer not to hop between dashboards)?
4) Timeline: would prefer a 3-week window if it helps with a more robust evaluation - we can extend to 3 weeks.

I'm attaching the sample_prompts.csv (first pass) and will follow up with Carlos for any additional labeling details.

Thanks - Alicia
Alicia Chen

Alicia - great, thanks for the sample CSV and questions. Quick clarifications below: 

- Latency: we'll measure P95 end-to-end from the Redwood endpoint in us-west (this excludes your last-mile client network). If you want us to add a synthetic client-side measurement we can instrument that too.
- Test set size: 200 items is fine - we'll use your 200-item set as the golden set for the trial.
- Datadog: yes - we support Datadog metrics export. To set this up we'll need a Datadog API key scoped for metrics ingestion; Marissa will coordinate the integration steps.
- Timeline: 3 weeks sounds reasonable and gives better statistical confidence. Proposed kickoff: Mon Jul 20, 09:00 PT. End date: Mon Aug 10.

Updated success criteria (adjusted for 200-item set):
- Latency: P95 <= 200 ms (short), P95 <= 450 ms (medium).
- Throughput: sustain 50 qps, <5% errors.
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0005.
- Quality: >= 90% pass rate on Atlas 200-item golden set; F1 drop <= 5% vs baseline.

I've created the HubSpot record: https://hubspot.example/deal/DEAL-2026-0812 - I'll attach the trial agreement to the record and send it for e-signature once you confirm.

- Redwood: provision trial environment and send keys + kickoff invite by Fri Jul 17 EOD.
